searchText: HI, There is a question. Only point_evaluation_precompile is deployed now, but our op project needs to upload original data during the challenge (not multi-round interactive). How can this re-uploaded original data be verified to be equal to the blob? Are you asking how to send blobs? https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4844#blob-transaction is used for that. NO, Blobs have already been sent in the previous transaction and versioned_ Hash saved the contract. Now I am sending another transaction again, which contains the same data as the blob in the previous transaction. I need to verify in the contract that the data in the second transaction is equivalent to the blob in the first transaction. You may just compare hashes, should be enough. (Seems like you need to save hash for blob from previous tx in the contract storage) Calculate the versioned hash in the contract and compare it with the previous one? It seems impossible Oh I see, you want to send blob via calldata in the second call, right? Yes, and verify that it is equivalent to the previous blob. This is the process Obstacle: How to use solidity verify verify (z, y) in polynomial. If you can verify that (z, y) exists in both blob and polynomial, then you can prove that data and blob are equivalent. Try passing z to polynomial in the contract to calculate y and compare it with y uploaded off-chain? Hi <@892053833121923094> <@755913785620824175> , we have this test: https://hivecancun.ethdevops.io/viewer.html?suiteid=1698232457-b8b2fa526e05d96e3960d3ecdeaf8560.json&suitename=engine-cancun&testid=197&showtestlog=1 which also fails locally. Suspicious lines are (in logs): ``` >> (5ffe76e2) {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":24,"method":"engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV3",... << (5ffe76e2) {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":24,"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"invalid argument 1 for key 'parentBeaconBlockRoot': argument must be a hex string"}} >> (5ffe76e2) {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":15,"method":"eth_getBlockByNumber","params":["latest",false]} << (5ffe76e2) {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":15,"result":{"number":"0x5", ... DEBUG (Invalid PayloadAttributes: Missing BeaconRoot): Forkchoice is applied even on invalid payload attributes ``` We reject the FCU, and if you check the (Syncing) variant we essentially do the same - but we pass that one. I can see that other clients do not have this behavior but I am also not sure what we are doing wrong here? 🤔 the test expects you to apply the forkchoice state in spite of invalid payloadAtrributes, there is a discussion thread on this problem: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/479 Ah great thanks 🙂 you're more than welcome to comment on that thread I will once I completely figure out what's going on and if I can add something to the discussion, thanks 🙂 And also thanks for the pointer to this one!

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content:
Hi <@892053833121923094> <@755913785620824175> , we have this test: https://hivecancun.ethdevops.io/viewer.html?suiteid=1698232457-b8b2fa526e05d96e3960d3ecdeaf8560.json&suitename=engine-cancun&testid=197&showtestlog=1 which also fails locally. Suspicious lines are (in logs):

```
>> (5ffe76e2) {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":24,"method":"engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV3",...
<< (5ffe76e2) {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":24,"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"invalid argument 1 for key 'parentBeaconBlockRoot': argument must be a hex string"}}
>> (5ffe76e2) {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":15,"method":"eth_getBlockByNumber","params":["latest",false]}
<< (5ffe76e2) {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":15,"result":{"number":"0x5", ...
DEBUG (Invalid PayloadAttributes: Missing BeaconRoot): Forkchoice is applied even on invalid payload attributes
```

We reject the FCU, and if you check the (Syncing) variant we essentially do the same - but we pass that one. I can see that other clients do not have this behavior but I am also not sure what we are doing wrong here? 🤔
